walkthroughs.body_html:
Urban Issues & Challenges — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Urban Issues & Challenges brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Urban Issues & Challenges.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What are Rio's informal settlements called?
options: Slums
Favelas
Bidonvilles
Townships

mcqs.q: Why do informal settlements develop in rapidly growing LIC cities?
options: Because the government forces them to move to cities.
Rural-urban migration outpaces formal housing supply; migrants build their own homes on marginal land without secure land tenure — driven by housing shortage, not by personal choice.
Informal settlements are built by the government for new migrants.
People live in slums because they prefer them or are too lazy to find better housing.

mcqs.q: Why do people move from rural to urban areas in LICs?
options: Because the government forces them to move to cities.
A combination of push factors (rural poverty, lack of services, agricultural change) and pull factors (perceived jobs, education, healthcare) — though reality often disappoints.
Informal settlements are built by the government for new migrants.
Because cities in poor countries are always better than the countryside.

mcqs.q: Why are urbanisation rates currently higher in LICs than HICs?
options: HICs urbanised earlier and are now near saturation (80%+ urban); LICs are still in the rapid urbanisation phase, with high rural-urban migration and urban natural increase.
Because the government forces them to move to cities.
Urbanisation only happens in LICs — HICs are deindustrialising.
LICs have higher urbanisation rates because they have more cities than HICs.
